item.title: Re: Seeking greenlight: Merit to Match
item.content:encoded:
I have mixed feelings about this one.
On one hand it does have an interesting spin on the self help genre, on the other it expresses a biased and harmful idea of justice and merit. The examples you gave made me cringe, being rich isn't a virtue and being poor isn't a character flaw. I suppose you gave these examples off the top of your head but if you take this forward I strongly recommend changing this. As it is this PoI isn't making much of a change in the world, they are just endorsing the current system and by the tone of their threat I feel like they want to shake things up.

item.title: Seeking greenlight: Merit to Match
item.content:encoded:
A bit of anomalous propaganda designed to make its own premise true: that people deserve where they end up in life.

I moved and trimmed your thread summary, since it was taking up extra space in the main forum screen. Try to keep thread descriptions (the text in the little box under the thread title) and titles short so you don't crowd out other authors in the forum listing. ~Zyn

Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Horror (?)

Elevator Pitch: A series of memetic ads/posts, detailing a philosophy about how to earn money and live a successful life (think the garage Lamborghini guy). The contained meme alters the personality of people exposed to it so that they deserve whatever they currently have (rich people become smart and diligent, poor people become delinquent and irresponsible, convicted people become violent and unstable, etc.). It is revealed to be funded by an anomalous entrepreneur with a message.

Central Narrative:

The Object Class is Neutralized, with a footnote explaining that non-anomalous lasting effects are still ongoing. The Foundation has already wiped the anomaly off the internet, and is investigating the PoI behind the anomaly. Nothing else can be done.

+ show block
– hide block

The description details the anomalous campaign's presence on social media and some of the text/videos it included. The memetic effects apply to anyone who watches one of the videos uninterrupted start to end. This alters their personality based on their present circumstances. (But the reveal of how comes later)

Discovery: The Foundation only discovers the anomalous properties of the ad campaign after it has existed for a few weeks and already gone moderately viral. It is discovered when a few Foundation researchers who watched the videos start performing noticeably better.

Tests are run on D-class, who don't seemingly experience any positive effects after exposure. Given its' beneficial effects on Level 1+ staff, the Foundation approves its experimental use on more researchers. In the weeks afterwards, the exposed D-class are discovered to be more hostile. One of them kills another D-class.

Conversation Log: The Foundation calls the maker of the campaign using a phone number in the ads and has a discussion with them. After the PoI realizes the Foundation is calling, they explain that the ad campaign is meant to promote "Justice" by creating a world in which more people deserve what they have, and more anecdotal evidence exists that peoples' character determines the circumstances where they end up. They promise they'll make more anomalies in the future and hang up.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The immediate hook is the Neutralized object class with the caveat attached, making the reader wonder what kind of damage has been done. For the first half of the article, the reader assumes the anomaly is "a self help ad campaign that makes people better", and then the actual nature of the anomaly comes as a twist/gut-punch.


As a courtesy to our readers on mobile devices, please collapse long posts. ~Zyn
